name: Vector Fields
miniText: What does a local direction field imply about a particle's trajectory? NetLogo Vector Fields displays arrows tangent to circles around the origin, with magnitude increasing with distance, and moves particles through finite direction-following steps. Differential geometry [1] supplies the language of curves and tangent directions; computer graphics [2] explains arrows and spatial encoding; Cabral and Leedom [3] provide a related field-visualization method using line integral convolution. The original Info identifies an important numerical artifact: trajectories slowly spiral outward because particles travel before recalculating their headings. Changing step size changes this approximation. The baseline illustrates an abstract vector field rather than identifying a particular gravitational or electromagnetic law. A circular-looking vector plot alone cannot establish force-based orbital motion, since velocity fields and acceleration fields imply different differential equations.
